questions.skill: Rotations and reflections that carry a rectangle, parallelogram, or trapezoid onto itself
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Rectangle ABCD is not a square. Describe every rotation (with angle greater than 0° and at most 360°) and every reflection that carries the rectangle onto itself.
questions.prompt_markup: Rectangle ABCD is not a square. Describe every rotation (with angle greater than 0° and at most 360°) and every reflection that carries the rectangle onto itself.
questions.correct_answer: Rotations: 180° and 360° about the center O. Reflections: across the line through the midpoints of AB and CD, and across the line through the midpoints of BC and DA.
questions.grading_note: Form required: both rotations and both reflections, with the center and the lines named. The diagonals are NOT lines of symmetry of a non-square rectangle, and a 90° turn does not work because the sides have different lengths.

questions.grading_note: The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so a 180° turn about their intersection swaps P with R and Q with S. A general parallelogram has no line of symmetry.

sections.skill: Use a symmetry to deduce congruent parts of the figure

branch.new_demand: Use the rigid motion that carries a figure onto itself to deduce which of its sides, angles, and diagonals are congruent.

questions.skill: Use a symmetry to deduce congruent parts of the figure
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Isosceles trapezoid ABCD (AB ∥ DC) is carried onto itself by the reflection across the line through the midpoints of AB and DC. Which vertex does A go to? Use this to name a pair of congruent angles.
questions.prompt_markup: Isosceles trapezoid ABCD (AB ∥ DC) is carried onto itself by the reflection across the line through the midpoints of AB and DC. Which vertex does A go to? Use this to name a pair of congruent angles.
questions.correct_answer: A goes to B (and D goes to C), so ∠DAB ≅ ∠CBA.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent answer naming A → B and a pair of base angles (∠D ≅ ∠C also accepted). A reflection keeps angle measures.
